Third, rightsize using Compute Optimizer, and move suitable workloads to Graviton. Fourth, use Spot for CI runners and stateless test fleets. Fifth, clean up waste: unattached EBS volumes, old snapshots, idle load balancers and NAT gateways in unused VPCs. Sixth, add guardrails. Set AWS Budgets per account with alerts, and use budget actions where they fit. Use SCPs to block very large instance types in dev OUs. Do not buy Savings Plans for hours you will switch off. Review the results monthly.
keyPoints: Tag policies and cost allocation tags for visibility
Schedule off-hours shutdown of EC2, RDS and container services
Rightsize, use Graviton, and use Spot for CI and test
Remove idle resources such as EBS volumes, snapshots and NAT gateways
Budgets, alerts and SCPs on instance types as guardrails

subjective.question: A CloudFormation stack with a Lambda-backed custom resource has stayed in CREATE_IN_PROGRESS for almost an hour, then fails. The Lambda logs show a Python exception. What happened, and how do you prevent it?
subjective.answer: CloudFormation waits for the custom resource to send a SUCCESS or FAILED response to the pre-signed S3 ResponseURL in the event. The function threw an exception before it sent any response, so CloudFormation kept waiting until the timeout. By default that wait can be up to an hour. Deletes and rollbacks can hang the same way. To prevent it, wrap the handler in try/except/finally so that it always sends a response, FAILED with a reason on error. Use the cfn-response module or a helper library, or use the CDK Provider framework, which handles responses for you. Set the ServiceTimeout property on the custom resource to a short value so failures surface quickly. Handle Create, Update and Delete events correctly. Delete must succeed even if the physical resource is already gone, or stack deletion gets stuck. Return a stable PhysicalResourceId, because changing it on update causes CloudFormation to delete the old resource. Also make sure the function has network access to S3 to send the response.
keyPoints: CloudFormation waits for a response to the pre-signed ResponseURL
An unhandled exception means no response, so the stack hangs until timeout
Always send FAILED in error handling, or use the Provider framework
Set ServiceTimeout and handle Delete idempotently
Keep PhysicalResourceId stable; the Lambda needs network access to S3

subjective.question: Spot the security mistakes in this CloudFormation snippet and rewrite the risky parts.

code.code:
Parameters:
  DBPassword:
    Type: String
    Default: Admin12345
Resources:
  AppDB:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties:
      Engine: mysql
      DBInstanceClass: db.t3.medium
      AllocatedStorage: 50
      MasterUsername: admin
      MasterUserPassword: !Ref DBPassword
      PubliclyAccessible: true
      StorageEncrypted: false
Outputs:
  Password:
    Value: !Ref DBPassword

subjective.answer: There are several problems. The password is a parameter with a hard-coded default, so it sits in the template and in source control. The parameter has no NoEcho, so it appears in plain text in the console and API. The Output publishes the password to anyone who can describe the stack. PubliclyAccessible: true exposes the database to the internet if the subnet routes allow it. StorageEncrypted is false, and it cannot be turned on in place later without restoring from a snapshot. There is no DeletionPolicy or Multi-AZ for a production database. To fix it, remove the parameter and the output and set ManageMasterUserPassword: true, so RDS creates and rotates the secret in Secrets Manager. Alternatively, use a dynamic reference such as '{{resolve:secretsmanager:prod/appdb:SecretString:password}}'. Set PubliclyAccessible: false, place the instance in private subnets with a DB subnet group and a restrictive security group, set StorageEncrypted: true with a KMS key, and add DeletionPolicy: Snapshot and MultiAZ: true. cfn-lint and cfn-guard rules in the pipeline can catch these problems automatically.
keyPoints: No passwords in parameter defaults or outputs; NoEcho is not enough
Use ManageMasterUserPassword or Secrets Manager dynamic references
Private subnets and PubliclyAccessible false
Turn on encryption at creation, because it cannot be added in place
Add cfn-guard or cfn-lint policy checks in the pipeline

subjective.question: Compare backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby and multi-site active/active. A payments API needs an RTO of 15 minutes and an RPO of under 1 minute, at reasonable cost. Which do you pick and how would you build it?
subjective.answer: Backup and restore is the cheapest option, but it has an RTO and RPO of hours. Pilot light keeps data replicated and the core pieces ready, but compute is off, so scaling up takes time. It is often tens of minutes and can be risky under pressure. Warm standby runs a smaller, fully working copy in the DR Region, so you only scale it up. Multi-site active/active serves traffic from both Regions and gives near-zero RTO, but it costs the most and is complex, especially for write conflicts. For a 15-minute RTO and under-1-minute RPO, I pick warm standby. Build it with an Aurora Global Database, which replicates with lag of about a second and allows promotion in about a minute, or DynamoDB global tables. Run a small ECS or Auto Scaling fleet in the second Region from the same IaC pipeline. Use Route 53 health checks or Application Recovery Controller for failover. Run regular game days, because an untested DR plan is only a hope.
keyPoints: Know the RTO and RPO of each strategy and their cost order
Warm standby meets 15 minutes and under 1 minute at moderate cost
Cross-Region data replication with Aurora Global Database or DynamoDB global tables
Deploy both Regions from the same IaC; failover with Route 53 or ARC
Test failover regularly

subjective.question: An engineer created a CloudWatch alarm on 'MemoryUtilization' for an EC2 Auto Scaling group, but it always shows INSUFFICIENT_DATA. A CPU alarm on the same group works. What is wrong and how do you fix it?
subjective.answer: EC2 does not publish memory or disk-space metrics by default, because the hypervisor cannot see inside the guest OS. CPU works because it is a default AWS/EC2 metric. Memory needs the CloudWatch agent on each instance, publishing to the CWAgent namespace with a metric such as mem_used_percent. To fix it, install the agent through the launch template user data or Systems Manager, store the agent configuration in SSM Parameter Store, and give the instance role the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy. Next, check that the alarm points to the right namespace, metric name and dimensions. With an Auto Scaling group, configure the agent to add the AutoScalingGroupName dimension with append_dimensions and aggregation_dimensions, or the alarm will not match any data. Also check the alarm period against the agent's collection interval, and set TreatMissingData on purpose. For example, use 'missing' or 'breaching' depending on whether no data should be treated as a problem.
keyPoints: Memory is not a default EC2 metric
Install the CloudWatch agent; publishes to the CWAgent namespace
The instance role needs CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy
Namespace and dimensions, including the ASG name, must match the alarm
Set TreatMissingData deliberately

subjective.question: GuardDuty reports that an EC2 instance in a production account is talking to a known crypto-mining domain. Put your incident response steps in order, and say what you would automate.
subjective.answer: 1. Triage. Confirm the finding, identify the instance, account and owner, and open an incident record, for example in Systems Manager Incident Manager. 2. Preserve evidence before you change anything. Take EBS snapshots, capture instance metadata and, if your tooling supports it, memory. Tag the instance as under investigation. 3. Contain. Replace its security groups with an isolation security group that has no inbound or outbound rules. Detach it from the Auto Scaling group and deregister it from target groups, so it is not terminated or replaced while you investigate. Revoke or rotate the instance role's sessions. 4. Investigate. Use CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and Amazon Detective to find the entry point and any lateral movement. 5. Eradicate and recover. Rebuild from a known-good AMI through the pipeline, patch the root cause and rotate credentials. 6. Do a post-incident review and add new controls. Automate steps 2 and 3 with an EventBridge rule on GuardDuty findings that calls Step Functions or SSM Automation. Keep a human approval step for high-impact actions.
keyPoints: Preserve evidence such as snapshots and tags before changes
Isolate with an empty security group; detach from the ASG and target groups
Revoke the credentials of the instance role
Investigate with CloudTrail, Flow Logs and Detective; rebuild from a clean AMI
Automate with EventBridge plus Step Functions or SSM Automation, with approval

subjective.question: Spot the mistake in this GitHub Actions deploy job for AWS and describe the better design.

code.code:
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          aws-region: ap-south-1
      - run: npx cdk deploy --all --require-approval never

subjective.answer: The job uses long-lived IAM user access keys stored as repository secrets. If they leak, they keep working until someone rotates them. They are usually over-privileged, and CloudTrail shows only the IAM user, not which workflow ran. Deploying every stack with --require-approval never also lets security-sensitive IAM changes go out without review. A better design is OIDC federation. Create an IAM OIDC identity provider for token.actions.githubusercontent.com and a deploy role whose trust policy checks the aud claim and limits the sub claim to the specific repository and branch or environment, such as repo:org/app:environment:prod. In the workflow, add 'permissions: id-token: write' and use role-to-assume with the role ARN. The job then gets short-lived credentials. Give the role least privilege, for example only permission to assume the CDK bootstrap roles. Use GitHub environments with required reviewers for production, and remove the IAM user.
keyPoints: Long-lived access keys are a leak risk and hard to audit
Use the GitHub OIDC provider with a role-to-assume
Restrict the trust policy by the sub claim for repository and branch or environment
Least privilege: allow only assuming the CDK bootstrap roles
Production approval gates instead of --require-approval never for all stacks

subjective.question: Finance wants each of 60 accounts and each product team to see its own AWS spend. Teams should get an alert before they overspend, and finance wants a monthly chargeback report. Design this end to end.
subjective.answer: Start with Organizations consolidated billing, so that volume discounts and Savings Plans are shared. The account structure itself gives a first level of cost split. Next, define mandatory tags such as CostCenter, Team and Environment. Enforce them with tag policies and with SCPs or IaC checks that deny untagged creates where they are supported. Activate them as cost allocation tags in the management or billing account. Use AWS Cost Categories to group accounts and tags into business units. For reporting, set up an AWS Data Export, the CUR 2.0 format, to S3 and query it with Athena or show it in QuickSight, using the Cloud Intelligence Dashboards if they fit. For alerts, create AWS Budgets per account or per cost category, with forecast-based alerts to team channels through SNS. Use budget actions where automatic limits are acceptable. Turn on Cost Anomaly Detection to catch sudden spikes. Decide how shared costs, such as networking and support, are split, and write the rule down so the chargeback is trusted.
keyPoints: Consolidated billing and an account-per-team structure
Tag policies and activated cost allocation tags; Cost Categories
Data Exports (CUR 2.0) to S3 with Athena or QuickSight
Budgets with forecast alerts and Cost Anomaly Detection
A documented rule for splitting shared costs

subjective.question: After a merger, the acquired company's data centre uses 10.0.0.0/16, which is the same range as your main production VPC. Both sides need to call a few of each other's services next month, and re-addressing will take a year. What are your options, and which is better here?
subjective.answer: Normal routing through Transit Gateway or Direct Connect cannot work, because the same prefix would exist on both sides. Option 1 is AWS PrivateLink. Put each service that must be shared behind an NLB and publish it as an endpoint service. Consumers create interface endpoints from their own address space, so the overlap does not matter. This works well for AWS-hosted services, and access is one-way for each service. Option 2 is a private NAT gateway. Add a non-overlapping secondary CIDR to the VPC, for example from 100.64.0.0/10, place a private NAT gateway in it, and route traffic to the other network through it. Traffic is translated to the non-overlapping range. Inbound calls can reach an ALB or NLB placed in the routable range. Option 3 is NAT on the on-premises firewalls, which is fine for a few flows but is fragile and needs manual work. For a few services in a month, I would use PrivateLink for AWS-hosted APIs and a private NAT gateway for outbound calls to the data centre. Then plan the re-addressing with VPC IPAM.
keyPoints: Overlapping CIDRs block routing through TGW and DX
PrivateLink avoids overlap for each service exposed
A private NAT gateway in a non-overlapping secondary CIDR handles outbound traffic
On-premises NAT works but is fragile
Long-term fix: re-addressing planned with VPC IPAM

steps.overview: This step covers the logistics that turn your preparation into a valid certificate. You will choose between online proctoring and a test centre, request the ESL +30 minute accommodation if eligible, book the exam, then claim your Credly badge and plan recertification. Mistakes here, like a name mismatch, a failed system check or forgetting the ESL request, can cost you the exam fee even if you know the content.
objectives: Choose between Pearson VUE online proctoring and a test centre based on your home setup and risk tolerance
Request the ESL +30 minute accommodation in your AWS Certification Account before scheduling an English-language exam
Book, reschedule or cancel an exam within the allowed windows without losing your fee
Claim your Credly digital badge and present the certification correctly on your résumé and LinkedIn
Plan recertification within the 3-year validity period and use the 50% voucher earned from each pass

concepts.explanation: This is your central portal for AWS exams. You schedule exams, request accommodations, view score reports, download certificates and find benefits such as the 50% voucher here. Your legal name in this account must exactly match your government photo ID.

AWS exams are delivered by Pearson VUE. You can take them in person at a Pearson VUE test centre or online from home or office through OnVUE online proctoring. The exam content, length and scoring are the same in both modes.

You take the exam on your own computer while a remote proctor watches through your webcam and microphone. You must pass a system test, show your room and desk, and stay alone and in camera view for the whole exam. Common failure causes are unstable internet, corporate laptops with blocked software, extra monitors, and background noise or people.

You sit the exam at a Pearson VUE centre on its controlled hardware and network. This removes the risk of home internet or system problems. It suits learners with noisy homes, shared rooms or unreliable power, which is common in many Indian cities.

Candidates whose native language is not English can request 30 extra minutes when they take an exam in English. You request it once in the AWS Certification Account under exam accommodations, and it applies to later exams. It must be approved before you schedule, because exams booked earlier do not get the extra time automatically.

Scores are reported from 100 to 1000. The pass mark is 700 for Foundational, 720 for Associate and 750 for Professional. Some questions are unscored and used for research, and you cannot tell which ones they are. The scoring is compensatory, so you do not need to pass each domain separately.

An AWS certification is valid for 3 years. You recertify by passing the current version of the same exam before your certification expires. Passing a higher-level exam can also recertify related lower-level certifications, as listed on AWS's recertification page.

After you pass, AWS sends an email from Credly so you can claim a verifiable digital badge. You can share the badge on LinkedIn and link it in your résumé so employers can confirm it is real and current.

keyFacts: Request ESL +30 minutes BEFORE booking. The extra time only applies to exams scheduled after approval.
Certifications are valid for 3 years from the date you pass. Recertify by passing the current exam version before expiry.
Each pass gives a 50% discount voucher for your next exam. You find it in the Benefits section of your AWS Certification Account.
Exam lengths: CLF-C02 and AIF-C01 are 90 minutes, Associates are 130 minutes, Professionals are 180 minutes. ESL adds 30 minutes to each.
Pass marks are 700 for Foundational, 720 for Associate and 750 for Professional, on a 100–1000 scale.
Reschedule or cancel more than 24 hours before the appointment to avoid losing your fee.
After a failed attempt you must wait 14 days before retaking, and you pay the full fee again.
Your ID name must exactly match your AWS Certification Account name. A mismatch can mean you are turned away and lose the fee.
Results are usually available in your account within 5 business days. The Credly badge email follows after the result is released.

example.caption: Worked plan: booking SAA-C03, then using the 50% voucher for DVA-C02
example.code:
Candidate: Priya, Pune, native language Marathi

Week 0 (before booking)
  1. AWS Certification Account -> Request accommodation -> ESL +30 min
  2. Wait for approval email
  3. Check that profile name = PAN/passport name (e.g. 'Priya S Kulkarni')

Week 0 (booking)
  4. Schedule SAA-C03 with Pearson VUE
     Mode: test centre (shared flat, unreliable Wi-Fi)
     Duration shown: 130 + 30 = 160 min  <- confirms ESL applied
     Fee: USD 150

Exam day
  5. Arrive early with original ID; no phone or notes at the desk
  6. Flag tough questions; answer every one (no negative marking)

After pass (score 780 / 720 needed)
  7. Claim Credly badge -> add to LinkedIn + résumé link
  8. Benefits -> 50% voucher
  9. Book DVA-C02: USD 150 x 50% = USD 75 (ESL still applies: 160 min)

Calendar reminders
  SAA-C03 expires 3 years after pass date
  Reminder at month 30: check current exam version, plan recert

pitfalls: Booking first and requesting ESL later. The existing booking keeps the standard time, so you would need to reschedule it.
Taking online proctoring on an office laptop with VPN, firewall or admin restrictions. Run the Pearson VUE system test on the exact machine and network you will use.
Using a nickname or leaving out a middle or initial name in your account when your ID shows the full name. Fix your profile name before exam day.
Reading aloud, looking away from the screen often, or letting someone walk into the room during an online exam. The proctor can end your exam without a refund.
Assuming the 50% voucher lasts forever or works on any vendor's exam. It applies to AWS exams only, so check its expiry in the Benefits section and use it in time.
Letting a certification lapse. Once it expires you must pass the exam again as a new candidate, so plan recertification months ahead.

files.code:
# exam-week-planner

Step 7 of 7: book, pass and keep it current.

## Real-world steps (the tool only plans them)
1. Sign in to your **AWS Certification Account** (aws.training, then Certification).
2. If English is not your native language, request the **ESL accommodation (+30 minutes)**
   under Accommodations **before** you schedule. It is not added to an exam you already booked.
3. Schedule with **Pearson VUE**. Choose one delivery mode:
   - **Online proctoring (OnVUE)**: run the system test, use a quiet private room and check in early.
   - **Test centre**: arrive early with your ID. The centre provides the computer.
4. Read the reschedule and cancel deadline in your confirmation email.
5. After the exam, your result shows in the Certification Account. The score is **scaled (100-1000)**.
   Some questions are **unscored**, and you cannot tell which ones, so answer every question.
6. Claim your **Credly** badge from the email, then add it to LinkedIn and your résumé.
7. Find your **50% discount voucher** under Benefits and use it for your next exam.
8. Certifications are valid for **3 years**. To recertify, pass the current version of the exam.
   Check the AWS recertification page for current rules about higher-level exams.

## Use the tool
- Edit `certs.json` with your own data.
- Run `python src/planner.py certs.json`.
- Exit code 1 means that you must act (for example, request ESL) before you book.
- Run `python src/resume.py certs.json` and paste the output into your résumé.

## Checkpoint
Your badge is claimed on Credly, and the résumé line from `resume.py` includes its link.

"""Exam-day checklists for the two Pearson VUE delivery modes."""

COMMON = [
    "Name in the AWS Certification Account matches your government photo ID exactly",
    "Confirmation email saved; note the reschedule/cancel deadline",
    "Answer every question: unscored items are mixed in and are not marked",
]

ONVUE = [  # online proctoring
    "Run the Pearson VUE OnVUE system test on the SAME computer and network",
    "Private, quiet room; clear desk; no second monitor, phone or notes in reach",
    "Stable internet and power; close VPN, chat and background apps",
    "Start check-in early: room photos, ID photo, face photo",
    "Stay in camera view; do not read questions aloud",
]

TEST_CENTRE = [
    "Confirm the centre address and travel time the day before",
    "Arrive early with your ID; lockers hold phones and bags",
    "Ask staff for a noteboard if you need one",
]


def checklist(delivery: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return the full checklist for 'onvue' or 'test_centre'."""
    modes = {"onvue": ONVUE, "test_centre": TEST_CENTRE}
    if delivery not in modes:
        raise ValueError(f"delivery must be one of {sorted(modes)}")
    return COMMON + modes[delivery]

"""Exam-week planner: ESL check, booking details, expiry and voucher reminders."""
import json
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

from checklist import checklist

PASS_MARKS = {"CLF-C02": 700, "AIF-C01": 700, "SAA-C03": 720, "DVA-C02": 720,
              "MLA-C01": 720, "DEA-C01": 720, "SAP-C02": 750, "DOP-C02": 750}
ESL_EXTRA_MINUTES = 30   # added only after AWS approves the accommodation
VALID_YEARS = 3          # every AWS certification is valid for 3 years
RECERT_WARN_DAYS = 180   # our own reminder window, not an AWS rule


def add_years(d: date, years: int) -> date:
    try:
        return d.replace(year=d.year + years)
    except ValueError:  # 29 Feb in a non-leap year
        return d.replace(year=d.year + years, day=28)


def exam_minutes(base: int, native_english: bool, esl_approved: bool) -> int | None:
    """Return exam length, or None if ESL must be requested before booking."""
    if native_english:
        return base
    return base + ESL_EXTRA_MINUTES if esl_approved else None


def main(path: str, today: date | None = None) -> int:
    today = today or date.today()
    data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    who, status, held = data["candidate"], 0, False
    for c in data["certifications"]:
        if "passed_on" in c:  # certification already held
            held = True
            expires = add_years(date.fromisoformat(c["passed_on"]), VALID_YEARS)
            left = (expires - today).days
            print(f"[HELD] {c['code']} {c['score']}/1000 (pass {PASS_MARKS[c['code']]}), expires {expires}, {left} days left")
            if left <= RECERT_WARN_DAYS:
                print("  -> Recertify: pass the CURRENT version of this exam before expiry")
            continue
        minutes = exam_minutes(c["base_minutes"], who["native_english"], who["esl_approved"])
        if minutes is None:
            print(f"[STOP] {c['code']}: request ESL +30 min in the AWS Certification Account BEFORE booking")
            status = 1
            continue
        print(f"[BOOK] {c['code']} on {c['exam_date']} via {c['delivery']}, {minutes} minutes, pass {PASS_MARKS[c['code']]}/1000")
        for item in checklist(c["delivery"]):
            print(f"  [ ] {item}")
    if held:
        print("[TIP] Use the 50% voucher from Benefits in your Certification Account for the next exam")
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "certs.json"))

"""Print a résumé 'Certifications' section with verifiable Credly links."""
import json
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

from planner import VALID_YEARS, add_years


def resume_lines(data: dict) -> list[str]:
    lines = ["CERTIFICATIONS"]
    for c in data["certifications"]:
        if "passed_on" not in c:
            continue  # list only exams you have passed
        passed = date.fromisoformat(c["passed_on"])
        expires = add_years(passed, VALID_YEARS)
        url = c.get("credly_url", "")
        if "REPLACE" in url or not url:
            url = "(claim your Credly badge first)"  # checkpoint not met yet
        lines.append(
            f"- {c['name']} ({c['code']}), {passed:%b %Y} - valid to {expires:%b %Y} | Verify: {url}"
        )
    return lines


if __name__ == "__main__":
    path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "certs.json"
    data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    print("\n".join(resume_lines(data)))

revision.examFocus: This step is not a scored exam domain. It covers the logistics that decide whether your preparation turns into a pass: delivery choice, ESL time, ID rules, scoring, recertification and benefits. No question tests this, but a wrong booking, ID or room setup can cost you the fee before you see question 1.

compare.difference: Online puts you in charge of the machine, network and room, and a proctor watches you on webcam. At a test centre, Pearson VUE controls the setup and you only control getting there on time with valid ID.
compare.chooseA: Choose online if you have a personal laptop with admin rights, a stable wired or strong Wi-Fi connection, a quiet private room with a clear desk, and you passed the system test on that exact setup.
compare.chooseB: Choose a test centre if your only machine is an office laptop with VPN or locked settings, your home is noisy or shared, power or internet is unreliable, or you want zero risk of a room-scan dispute.

compare.a: Reschedule or cancel (more than 24 hours before)
compare.difference: Rescheduling an appointment you have not sat costs nothing if you do it in time. A retake is a new attempt, allowed only after 14 days, and you pay the full fee again.
compare.chooseA: Reschedule if your mock scores are not ready, you get sick, or you forgot to request ESL before booking, as long as you are outside the 24-hour window.
compare.chooseB: Plan a retake only after a fail. Use the score report's section feedback to target weak domains during the 14-day wait.

compare.difference: The voucher halves the fee of your next AWS exam only. It has an expiry date, so it is wasted if you sit your next exam after that date.
compare.chooseA: Apply the voucher at checkout when your next AWS exam falls before its expiry, for example AIF-C01 or an Associate after CLF-C02.
compare.chooseB: Pay full price only if the voucher has expired or was already used. Check Benefits first every time.

compare.difference: The badge is a shareable, verifiable link for LinkedIn and your résumé. The PDF and validation number in your AWS Certification Account are what employers or partners may ask for as formal proof.
compare.chooseA: Use the Credly badge link on LinkedIn, résumés and email signatures so recruiters can verify it in one click.
compare.chooseB: Use the PDF or validation number when an employer's HR or an AWS Partner programme asks for official proof.

compare.a: Recertify by passing the current version
compare.b: Let it lapse and start again
compare.difference: Recertifying before expiry keeps the certification continuous with a new 3-year validity. After expiry you hold nothing and must sit the exam as a new candidate.
compare.chooseA: Recertify if the certification matters for your job, a partner tier or a client requirement. Book it months before the expiry date.
compare.chooseB: Letting it lapse is acceptable only if you have moved to a path where it no longer adds value. Check whether a higher-level pass in the same path recertifies it under current AWS policy.

cues.cue: Office laptop, corporate VPN, cannot install software
cues.pick: Test centre, or a personal machine that passed the system test
cues.why: OnVUE needs its secure browser to run and connect freely, and corporate controls often block it on exam day.

cues.cue: English is not my first language
cues.pick: Request the ESL +30 minutes in your account before you book
cues.why: Bookings made before approval keep the standard time, so you would have to reschedule them.

cues.cue: My ID says 'Venkata Ramana Rao K' but my account says 'Ramana Rao'
cues.pick: Edit the account name to match the ID before exam day
cues.why: A name mismatch at check-in can mean you are turned away and lose the fee.

cues.cue: I failed by a small margin yesterday
cues.pick: Wait 14 days, revise weak domains from the score report, pay again or use any valid voucher
cues.why: No retake is allowed inside 14 days, and a fail is not refunded.

cues.cue: I passed CLF-C02, what next?
cues.pick: Claim the Credly badge, then book the next exam with the 50% voucher before it expires
cues.why: The voucher is the cheapest route to AIF-C01 or an Associate, and it is lost if unused.

cues.cue: My certification expires in four months
cues.pick: Book the current version of the exam now
cues.why: Recertifying before expiry keeps continuity, and a late fail leaves no time for a 14-day retake.

cues.cue: I'm stuck on a question I can't answer
cues.pick: Pick the best guess, flag it, move on
cues.why: There is no negative marking, some questions are unscored, and time lost on one item hurts more than a guess.

scenario.situation: Priya, an engineer in Pune whose first language is Marathi, booked SAA-C03 online for next Saturday on her office laptop. Her company uses a mandatory VPN and she has no admin rights. Her account shows 'Priya S' while her PAN and passport show 'Priya Suresh Kulkarni'. She has not requested ESL. It is Monday. What should she do first to protect her attempt?
reasoning: Every issue is fixable because she is well outside the 24-hour window. So rescheduling costs nothing now, while waiting risks losing the fee.
ESL time is not added to an existing booking. She should request the accommodation first, wait for approval, then reschedule so the new appointment gets 160 minutes instead of 130.
The office laptop with VPN and no admin rights is a high-risk setup for OnVUE. She should either run the system test on a personal machine on her home network, or switch to a Pune test centre.
The name 'Priya S' does not match her ID. She must update the account to 'Priya Suresh Kulkarni' to match the ID she will present.
Doing nothing, or only running the system test, leaves the ESL and ID problems in place. So the correct first move covers all three issues.
scenario.answer: Update her account name to match her ID and request ESL now. Once ESL is approved, reschedule to a date that gets the extra time, on a personal machine that passes the system test or at a test centre. This fixes the time, identity and technology risks while rescheduling is still free.

memoryAids: Before booking, think 'N-E-T': Name matches ID, ESL approved, Test (system test) passed on the exam machine.
Exam times '90-130-180, plus 30': Foundational, Associate, Professional, with ESL adding 30 to each (120, 160, 210).
Pass marks '700-720-750: climb by 20, then 30': Foundational, Associate, Professional.
cheatSheet: Request ESL first and book second. Confirm the accommodation shows in your account before each booking.
ESL times: CLF-C02 and AIF-C01 go to 120 minutes, Associates to 160, Professionals to 210.
Scaled score of 100–1000 with pass marks of 700, 720 and 750. Scoring is compensatory, so you do not need to pass each domain separately.
Some questions are unscored and not marked as such. Treat every question as if it counts.
No negative marking: never leave a question blank, and flag items to review if time allows.
OnVUE: private room, clear desk, no second screen, no talking or reading aloud, eyes on screen, nobody walks in.
Run the Pearson VUE system test on the exact laptop, network and room you will use, ideally a day before and again on exam day.
Check in early. Online check-in includes photos of your ID and room, and lateness can forfeit the appointment.
Reschedule or cancel more than 24 hours before the appointment. After that you lose the fee.
Fail: 14-day wait, full fee again, and use the score report's domain feedback to plan revision.
Pass: result usually within 5 business days, then the Credly email. Accept the badge, add it to LinkedIn and your résumé, and note the 3-year expiry.
Use the 50% voucher from Benefits before it expires. It is valid for AWS exams only, and one voucher covers one exam.
selfCheck: I can choose between online proctoring and a test centre for my own laptop, network and home, and justify the choice.
I can list the exact order of actions before booking: fix my name, get ESL approved, run the system test, then book.
I can state the standard and ESL time and the pass mark for the exam I am taking.
I can explain what happens if I miss the 24-hour window, fail, or let my certification expire.
I can find and apply my 50% voucher and state its expiry date.
I can show my accepted Credly badge on LinkedIn and my résumé, and I have put a recertification reminder in my calendar.

objective.question: Priya is a non-native English speaker. She plans to take SAA-C03 and wants the ESL accommodation. What should she do first?
options: Book the exam and email AWS Support within 24 hours to add the extra time
Choose a test centre, because ESL only applies to test centre delivery
Request the ESL accommodation in her AWS Certification Account, wait for approval, then book the exam
Book the exam, then request ESL from the Pearson VUE proctor on exam day
objective.explanation: ESL (+30 minutes) must be requested and approved before you schedule, because the extra time only applies to exams booked after approval. Proctors cannot add time on exam day, and ESL is not limited to test centres.

objective.question: Rahul booked DVA-C02 for next week. Two days later his ESL accommodation was approved. What happens to his existing appointment?
options: It gets 15 extra minutes because approval came after booking
It keeps the standard 130 minutes; to get the extra time he must reschedule or cancel and rebook after approval
The appointment is cancelled by AWS and the fee is refunded
It automatically gets 30 extra minutes
objective.explanation: Extra time applies only to exams scheduled after approval, so the existing booking stays at 130 minutes. He should rebook more than 24 hours before the appointment to avoid losing the fee.

objective.question: A candidate with approved ESL accommodation books SAP-C02. How long will the exam appointment be?
options: 210 minutes
160 minutes
200 minutes
180 minutes
objective.explanation: Professional exams are 180 minutes, and ESL adds 30 minutes, giving 210 minutes. The other options use the wrong base time or the wrong extra time.

objective.question: Which pairing of exam and passing scaled score is correct?
objective.explanation: Associate exams such as DEA-C01 need 720 on a 100–1000 scale. Foundational exams (CLF-C02, AIF-C01) need 700, and Professional exams (DOP-C02, SAP-C02) need 750.

objective.question: Anita passed SAA-C03 on 10 March 2026. Which statement about her certification is correct?
options: It is valid for 3 years from 10 March 2026, and she recertifies by passing the current version before it expires
It is valid for life as long as she claims the Credly badge
It is valid until the end of the 2029 calendar year, whatever her pass date
It is valid for 2 years and renews automatically if she keeps her account active
objective.explanation: AWS certifications are valid for 3 years from the date you pass. You keep them active by passing the current exam version before expiry; nothing renews automatically.

objective.question: After passing CLF-C02, where does a candidate find the 50% discount voucher for the next exam?
options: In the Benefits section of the AWS Certification Account
In the AWS Billing console under Credits
On the printed score report at the test centre
In the Credly badge email
objective.explanation: The 50% voucher earned from passing is shown in the Benefits section of the AWS Certification Account. It is not in Credly, a score report, or the AWS Billing console.

objective.question: Karthik's MLA-C01 exam is booked for Friday at 10:00. Something urgent comes up. Which action protects his exam fee?
options: Rescheduling or cancelling before Thursday 10:00, i.e. more than 24 hours before the appointment
Rescheduling up to 1 hour before the exam starts
Calling the test centre on Friday morning to move the slot
Simply not attending; the fee carries over automatically
objective.explanation: You must reschedule or cancel more than 24 hours before the appointment to avoid losing the fee. A no-show or a late change means the fee is lost.

objective.question: Meera failed DEA-C01 on 1 June. Which statement about her retake is correct?
options: She must wait 14 days and pay the full exam fee again
She can use the 50% pass voucher for the retake
She must wait 30 days, but the retake is free
She can retake the next day at half price
objective.explanation: After a failed attempt you must wait 14 days before retaking, and you pay the full fee again. The 50% voucher is earned only by passing, so she does not have one from this attempt.

objective.question: Arjun's passport says 'Arjun Kumar Reddy', but his AWS Certification Account profile says 'Arjun Reddy'. His exam is in a week. What is the best action?
options: Bring a second ID with a shorter name
Tell the proctor about the difference at check-in
Update the AWS Certification Account name to exactly match his ID before the exam
Do nothing; proctors accept partial name matches
objective.explanation: Your ID name must exactly match your AWS Certification Account name. A mismatch can mean you are turned away and lose the fee, so fix it well before exam day rather than relying on the proctor.

objective.question: On an Associate exam with 65 questions, a candidate notices some questions feel unusually unfamiliar. Which statement about scoring is correct?
options: Some questions are unscored and used to test future content; they are not marked, so candidates should answer every question with full effort
Every question is scored and raw marks are converted to a percentage
Unscored questions are labelled 'beta' so you can skip them
Unfamiliar questions carry double marks
objective.explanation: AWS exams include unscored questions that do not affect your result, and they are not identified. Results are reported as a scaled score from 100 to 1000, not a raw percentage.

objective.question: Which statement best describes how AWS reaches a pass or fail result?
options: Your overall scaled score is compared with the pass mark; it is a compensatory model, so strong domains can offset weak ones
Only the highest-weighted domain decides the result
Wrong answers carry negative marking, so you should leave unsure questions blank
You must pass every domain separately
objective.explanation: AWS uses a compensatory scoring model: you pass on the overall scaled score, not domain by domain. There is no penalty for guessing, so blank answers simply count as incorrect.

objective.question: Sandeep lives in a shared flat with frequent power cuts and unstable Wi-Fi. He wants the lowest risk of his exam being interrupted. Which delivery option suits him best?
options: A Pearson VUE test centre
Online proctoring using his phone's mobile hotspot as the only connection
Online proctoring from a café with public Wi-Fi
Online proctoring (OnVUE) from his bedroom
objective.explanation: A test centre provides a controlled room, hardware and network, which removes home power and connectivity risks. Online proctoring needs a private, quiet room and a stable connection; cafés and public spaces are not allowed.

objective.question: Which practice is correct when preparing for an online proctored (OnVUE) AWS exam?
options: Run the Pearson VUE system test on the same computer and network you will use, and clear your desk and room
Use a work laptop with a corporate VPN and firewall turned on
Have a family member sit in the room to help with technical problems
Keep a second monitor connected so you can view notes
objective.explanation: The system test confirms that your webcam, microphone, bandwidth and computer work with OnVUE. Extra monitors, other people in the room and restrictive corporate VPN or firewall settings can stop or invalidate the session.

objective.question: Neha finished CLF-C02 yesterday. When should she expect her result and Credly badge?
options: Both arrive by post within 3 weeks
She must ask the proctor to email the result
The result is usually in her AWS Certification Account within 5 business days, and the Credly badge email follows after the result is released
The badge arrives first; the result follows a month later
objective.explanation: Results are usually available in your AWS Certification Account within 5 business days. The Credly badge email comes only after the result is released.

objective.question: Vikram passed SAA-C03 and has his 50% voucher. He now books DOP-C02 (USD 300) and uses the voucher. Assuming no taxes, what does he pay, and what does he get if he passes DOP-C02?
options: USD 150; a new 50% voucher for his next exam
USD 150; a free exam voucher
USD 300; the voucher only applies to Associate exams
USD 75; no further voucher
objective.explanation: The voucher takes 50% off the next exam, so USD 300 becomes USD 150. Each pass gives a new 50% voucher, so passing DOP-C02 earns another one, not a free exam.

objective.question: On SAA-C03, a multiple-response question asks the candidate to choose TWO answers. The candidate selects one correct option and one incorrect option. How is this question scored?
options: It earns no credit because all correct responses must be selected
It earns full credit if the correct option is listed first
It is converted to an unscored question
It earns half credit because one option is correct
objective.explanation: AWS gives credit for a multiple-response question only when all the correct responses are selected. There is no partial credit, and answer order does not matter.

objective.question: A candidate has 4 minutes left on DVA-C02 and 6 questions still unanswered. Which action gives the best chance of a higher score?
options: Select an answer for every remaining question, because unanswered questions are scored as incorrect
End the exam early so the unanswered questions become unscored
Answer only the ones he is sure of and skip the rest
Leave them blank, because wrong answers carry a negative mark
objective.explanation: AWS exams have no penalty for guessing, and a blank answer is simply scored as incorrect. A guess can only help. Ending the exam early never turns questions into unscored ones.

objective.question: Deepa got the ESL accommodation approved before booking SAA-C03 last year. She now wants to book MLA-C01. What must she do to get the extra 30 minutes?
options: Email Pearson VUE with a copy of her previous approval
Book the test centre option, because ESL is not available online
Nothing more. The approved ESL accommodation stays on her AWS Certification Account and applies to later eligible bookings
Submit a new ESL request for every exam
objective.explanation: ESL is a one-time request on the AWS Certification Account. Once it is approved, it applies to exams booked after the approval. It is available for both online and test centre delivery.

objective.question: Suresh's SAA-C03 certification expired three weeks ago. He missed the recertification reminder emails. What is his situation?
options: His certification and Credly badge are no longer active. He must pass the current version of the exam to become certified again
His certification is automatically extended because he holds Cloud Practitioner
He can pay a renewal fee to extend the certification without an exam
AWS gives a 90-day grace period, so he can still recertify without losing status
objective.explanation: An AWS certification expires 3 years after it is earned. There is no paid renewal and no grace period for the credential. To become certified again, he must pass the current exam version. A lower-level certification does not extend a higher one.

objective.question: A candidate earned a certification in 2023 on an exam version that AWS has since retired and replaced. The certification is now due for renewal. How does she recertify?
options: Pass the current version of that exam that is live when she books
Submit proof of work experience to AWS Training and Certification
Complete a free online course instead of an exam
Retake the retired version, because recertification must match the original version
objective.explanation: Recertification means passing the current version of the exam. Retired versions cannot be booked. Courses and work experience do not renew a certification.

objective.question: Ravi plans to take an OnVUE exam on his company laptop. The laptop runs a corporate VPN, endpoint security software and a restricted admin policy. The OnVUE system test keeps failing. What is the best fix?
options: Use a personal computer without corporate restrictions, and run the system test on the same computer and network well before exam day
Install a second webcam to satisfy the proctor
Run the system test again on exam day and hope it passes
Keep the VPN on, because it encrypts the exam traffic
objective.explanation: VPNs, firewalls and locked-down corporate builds often block the OnVUE secure browser. The reliable fix is an unrestricted personal machine that has passed the system test in advance on the same network. Extra hardware does not solve software blocks.

objective.question: AIF-C01 can include ordering and matching question types. A candidate gets an ordering question with 4 steps and puts 3 of them in the correct positions. How is it scored?
options: Full credit, because most of the steps are right
No credit. The full sequence must be correct to earn credit
It depends on the candidate's score in that domain
75% credit for the 3 correct positions
objective.explanation: AWS scores ordering and matching questions as all-or-nothing. There is no partial credit, so the whole sequence must be correct. Treat these questions with the same care as multiple-response questions.

objective.question: A recruiter in Bengaluru wants to confirm that a candidate's AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate certification is real and still active. What is the most reliable way to check?
options: Open the candidate's Credly badge link, or use AWS's certification validation with the validation number
Search for the candidate's name in the AWS Management Console
Call Pearson VUE customer support
Ask the candidate for a screenshot of the score report
objective.explanation: Credly badges carry issuer-verified details and show whether the badge is active or expired. AWS also supports validation using the candidate's validation number. Screenshots can be faked, and Pearson VUE and the AWS console do not verify certifications for third parties.

objective.question: Read the score report summary below. What does it mean?

code.code:
Exam: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03)
Scaled score: 742
Result: PASS

Section performance:
Design Secure Architectures ............ Meets competencies
Design Resilient Architectures ......... Meets competencies
Design High-Performing Architectures ... Needs improvement
Design Cost-Optimized Architectures .... Meets competencies

options: The result is provisional until the weak section is retaken
The 'Needs improvement' section was made of unscored questions
The candidate passed overall. Scoring is compensatory, so a weak section can be offset by stronger ones, and that section is still worth revising
The candidate failed, because one section needs improvement
objective.explanation: AWS uses a compensatory model: only the total scaled score has to meet the pass mark of 720, not each section. Section feedback is only a guide for further study. It does not show which questions were unscored.

objective.question: A non-native English speaker wants the ESL accommodation for SAA-C03 and plans to take it online. Which order of steps is correct?

code.code:
A. Schedule the exam with Pearson VUE
B. Sign in to the AWS Certification Account and check the profile name matches your ID
C. Request the ESL accommodation (+30 minutes)
D. Wait for the accommodation to be approved
E. Run the OnVUE system test on the exact machine and network you will use

options: A, B, C, D, E
C, B, A, D, E
B, A, C, D, E
B, C, D, A, E
objective.explanation: The account and name must be correct first. ESL must be approved before you book, because an existing booking keeps the standard time. The system test comes last, on the real exam setup. Every other order books the exam before ESL is approved, or requests ESL before the account is ready.

objective.question: Spot the mistake in this exam-week plan for an OnVUE exam.

code.code:
Mon: ESL already approved; book OnVUE for Sat 10:00, apply 50% voucher
Tue: Run OnVUE system test on personal laptop, home Wi-Fi - PASS
Wed: Update profile name to 'Kavya Lakshmi Iyer' to match passport
Fri: Home is noisy, so decide to take the exam on the office laptop at the office
Sat 09:30: Start check-in

options: Monday: a voucher cannot be applied to an OnVUE booking
Saturday: check-in at 09:30 is too early for a 10:00 exam
Wednesday: a profile name cannot be changed after booking
Friday: the system test was never run on the office laptop and office network
objective.explanation: The system test only proves that the tested machine and network work. An office laptop may have a VPN, a firewall or admin restrictions that block OnVUE. Vouchers work for online bookings, fixing the name before exam day is correct, and check-in opens 30 minutes before the start time.

objective.question: Twenty minutes into an OnVUE exam, Rohan needs the washroom. What happens if he leaves the webcam view?
options: The timer pauses automatically until he returns
He gets one scheduled 10-minute break on Associate exams
He may leave if he tells the proctor in chat first
Online proctored AWS exams do not allow breaks, so leaving the camera view can end the exam
objective.explanation: AWS does not allow breaks during online proctored exams. Leaving the camera view is a policy breach, and the proctor can end the exam. Plan for this before check-in. The timer does not pause, and there are no scheduled breaks.

objective.question: Pooja's CLF-C02 certification expires in four months. She also wants a new certification on her résumé. Which action both recertifies CLF-C02 and adds a new certification?
options: Complete an AWS Skill Builder course on cloud concepts
Pay a recertification fee in the AWS Certification Account
Renew the Credly badge from her Credly profile
Pass SAA-C03 before CLF-C02 expires
objective.explanation: Passing any Associate or Professional exam recertifies the Cloud Practitioner certification, and it also earns the new certification. Courses, Credly actions and fees do not recertify anything. Only passing an exam does.

objective.question: Imran holds SAA-C03, which expires in five months. He is already preparing for SAP-C02. What is the most efficient plan?
options: Pass SAA-C03 again first, then SAP-C02, because Professional exams do not recertify Associates
Pass SAP-C02 after SAA-C03 expires. It will reactivate the expired Associate
Let SAA-C03 expire. A Professional certification makes the Associate unnecessary
Pass SAP-C02 before the SAA-C03 expiry date. This earns the Professional certification and also recertifies the Associate
objective.explanation: Passing a Professional exam in the same path recertifies the related Associate, but only while the Associate is still active. After expiry, nothing reactivates it. You would have to pass that exam again as a new candidate.

objective.question: Lakshmi's Developer – Associate certification is due for renewal. Apart from passing the current DVA-C02 again, which exam would also recertify it?
options: DEA-C01 (Data Engineer – Associate)
MLA-C01 (Machine Learning Engineer – Associate)
SAP-C02 (Solutions Architect – Professional)
DOP-C02 (DevOps Engineer – Professional)
objective.explanation: The DevOps Engineer – Professional certification sits above Developer – Associate, so passing it recertifies Developer – Associate. SAP-C02 recertifies the Solutions Architect – Associate. DEA-C01 and MLA-C01 are separate Associates and do not recertify DVA.

objective.question: Arvind passed SAA-C03 and received one 50% voucher. He wants to book both DVA-C02 and DEA-C01 at half price. What is true?
options: He can split the voucher into two 25% discounts
The voucher discounts both exams if he books them in the same session
The voucher discounts every AWS exam he books until it expires
The voucher is single-use, so it discounts only one of the two exams
objective.explanation: Each pass gives one single-use 50% voucher. If he passes DVA-C02 with the voucher, that pass gives him a new voucher he can use for DEA-C01. The voucher cannot be split or reused.

objective.question: Sneha reached her Pearson VUE test centre on time but was turned away. Her profile name matched her passport exactly. What is the most likely cause?
options: She had not run the OnVUE system test
She had not claimed her previous Credly badge
She had used a 50% voucher for the booking
Her passport had expired the month before
objective.explanation: Test centres require a valid, unexpired government-issued photo ID with a name that matches the booking. The OnVUE system test applies only to online exams. Credly status and vouchers have no effect on admission.

objective.question: A candidate with an approved ESL accommodation sits an Associate exam (65 questions). What is the average time available per question?
options: About 3.0 minutes
About 1.4 minutes
About 2.0 minutes
About 2.5 minutes
objective.explanation: An Associate exam is 130 minutes, plus 30 minutes for ESL, which gives 160 minutes. 160 divided by 65 is about 2.46 minutes per question. Keep some of that for a final review of flagged questions.

objective.question: Farhan's OnVUE exam starts at 15:00. When should he start the check-in process?
options: At exactly 15:00, because check-in time is taken from the exam time
At 14:58, after closing all other apps
At any time up to 15 minutes after the start time, with no risk
When the check-in window opens, 30 minutes before the start time
objective.explanation: Check-in opens 30 minutes early. It includes ID photos, room photos and a proctor review, and this takes time. If you start late, you risk being marked a no-show and losing the fee.

objective.question: Review this OnVUE room setup. Which item must change before check-in?

code.code:
- Desk cleared except laptop, mouse and passport
- External second monitor unplugged and switched off
- Mobile phone on a shelf behind me, out of arm's reach
- Wireless earbuds in to block out street noise
- Door closed, family told not to enter for 3 hours

options: The unplugged second monitor
The phone on the shelf
The closed door
The wireless earbuds
objective.explanation: Headphones and earbuds are not allowed during an online proctored exam. An unplugged monitor, a phone out of reach and a closed, private room all meet OnVUE rules.

objective.question: Ajay passed AIF-C01 a week ago. His AWS Certification Account shows the certification, but he has no Credly email. What is the most likely cause and fix?
options: He must pay a separate Credly fee to release the badge
Badges are only issued after the 50% voucher is used
Credly badges are only issued for Associate and Professional exams
The invitation went to the email address on his Certification Account, which differs from his usual inbox. He should check that address and its spam folder, then accept the badge
objective.explanation: Credly sends the badge invitation to the email linked to the AWS Certification Account. If he uses another email for Credly, he can add both addresses to his Credly account. All AWS certifications, including Foundational ones, issue free badges with no conditions.

objective.question: Nisha's SAA-C03 certification is valid until December 2026. She passes the current SAA-C03 exam again in August 2026. What is her new expiry date?
options: December 2029, three years added to the old expiry date
August 2027, one year from the recertification date
December 2026, unchanged until it expires
August 2029, three years from the date she recertified
objective.explanation: When you recertify, the new validity runs three years from the date you pass the recertification exam. It is not added to the old expiry date. This is why passing very early gives up a few months of validity.

objective.question: Gautam tries to apply his 50% voucher while booking MLA-C01, but it is rejected. Based on his Benefits page, what is the cause?

code.code:
Benefits
Exam discount voucher: 50% off
Earned: CLF-C02 pass
Status: Expired
Expiry date: 2026-01-31
Today: 2026-03-04

options: MLA-C01 is not eligible because vouchers work only on the next exam in the same level
Vouchers can only be used at test centres
He must first claim his Credly badge to unlock the voucher
The voucher expired before he tried to use it
objective.explanation: The status shows the voucher expired on 31 January 2026. Vouchers have an expiry date and cannot be extended. A valid voucher works on any AWS exam, through either delivery method, and does not depend on Credly.

objective.question: Spot the mistake in this résumé section, written in March 2026.

code.code:
CERTIFICATIONS
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) | Passed Feb 2026 | Valid until Feb 2029 | Credly link
AWS Certified Developer – Associate | Passed Jan 2022 | Active | Not recertified
AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) | Passed Nov 2025 | Valid until Nov 2028

options: The SAA-C03 line: Associate certifications are valid for two years
Credly links should not appear on a résumé
The AIF-C01 line: Foundational certifications do not expire
The Developer – Associate line: a 2022 pass that was never recertified expired in January 2025, so it cannot be shown as Active
objective.explanation: Certifications are valid for three years. The Developer – Associate certification lapsed in January 2025, and listing it as Active is misleading because recruiters can verify it. The other validity dates are correct, and Credly links help verification.

objective.question: Tanvi is a non-native English speaker. Her home has frequent power cuts and weak broadband. She has a valid 50% voucher and wants to sit SAA-C03 in three weeks. Which plan meets all her needs?
options: Book a test centre slot now and request ESL, which will be added automatically
Book OnVUE, keep a mobile hotspot ready, and skip ESL to save time
Book OnVUE now with the voucher, then request ESL tomorrow
Request ESL, wait for approval, then book a Pearson VUE test centre slot and apply the voucher during payment
objective.explanation: ESL must be approved before booking, or the booking keeps the standard time. A test centre removes the power and internet risk, and the voucher is applied while paying for the booking. Each of the other plans breaks at least one of these needs.

subjective.question: Compare online proctoring (OnVUE) with a Pearson VUE test centre. How would you choose between them?
subjective.answer: Both are delivered by Pearson VUE, and the exam content and scoring are the same. Online proctoring lets me sit at home, often with more slot choices. It needs a private, quiet room, a clear desk, a working webcam and microphone, and a stable internet connection. I must pass the system test on the same machine and network. A proctor watches me throughout, and things like noise, someone entering the room or looking away can end the session. A test centre removes these risks because the room, computer and network are controlled. The cost is travel and fewer slots. I choose a test centre if my home has power cuts, shared rooms or weak internet. I choose online if I have a reliable private setup and want flexibility.
keyPoints: Same exam and scoring through Pearson VUE
OnVUE needs a private room, clear desk, webcam, stable internet and a passed system test
Test centre gives a controlled environment but needs travel
Choose based on the risk in your home setup

subjective.question: Explain the ESL accommodation process and why the order of steps matters.
subjective.answer: If English is not my first language, I can request the ESL accommodation, which adds 30 minutes to the exam. I request it in my AWS Certification Account and wait for approval. Only then do I book the exam. The order matters because the extra time applies only to exams scheduled after approval. If I book first, that appointment keeps the standard time. So CLF-C02 stays at 90 minutes instead of 120, and SAA-C03 stays at 130 instead of 160. If I booked too early, I would reschedule or cancel more than 24 hours before the appointment and rebook after approval, so I do not lose the fee. For a 180-minute Professional exam, the extra 30 minutes is very valuable because the questions are long scenarios.
keyPoints: ESL adds 30 minutes for non-native English speakers
Request in the AWS Certification Account and get approval before booking
Extra time applies only to exams scheduled after approval
Fix an early booking by rescheduling more than 24 hours ahead

subjective.question: How does AWS scaled scoring work, and what are unscored questions? What does this mean for exam strategy?
subjective.answer: AWS reports results on a scaled score from 100 to 1000. The pass mark is 700 for Foundational, 720 for Associate and 750 for Professional. Scaling keeps results fair across different versions of the same exam, which may differ slightly in difficulty. So a scaled score is not a simple percentage. Each exam also includes some unscored questions that AWS uses to test future content. They do not affect my result, and they are not marked, so I cannot tell which ones they are. The model is compensatory, so I pass on my overall score, not domain by domain. There is no negative marking. My strategy is to answer every question, never leave one blank, treat every question as if it counts, and not panic if some questions look unusual.
keyPoints: Scaled score 100–1000; pass at 700/720/750 by level
Scaling keeps different exam forms fair
Unscored questions exist and are not identified
Compensatory model with no negative marking, so answer everything

subjective.question: Interview question: Your AWS Solutions Architect – Associate certification expires next month. What do you do?
subjective.answer: First I check the exact expiry date in my AWS Certification Account. The certification is valid for 3 years from my pass date. To keep it active, I must pass the current version of the exam before that date. I would check the current exam guide, because services and domains change between versions, and plan focused revision on anything new. Then I would book early enough to allow for a retake. If I fail, I must wait 14 days and pay the full fee again, so booking in the final week is risky. I would also check my Benefits section for a 50% voucher from an earlier pass. I would confirm that my ID still matches my account name. After passing, my validity resets and Credly updates the badge.
keyPoints: Validity is 3 years from the pass date; check it in the account
Recertify by passing the current version before expiry
Leave room for the 14-day retake wait
Use an available 50% voucher and confirm the ID matches

subjective.question: How would you use the 50% voucher to reduce the cost of a certification path from Cloud Practitioner to Solutions Architect – Professional?
subjective.answer: Each pass gives a 50% voucher for the next exam, and it appears in the Benefits section of my AWS Certification Account. On a path of CLF-C02, then SAA-C03, then SAP-C02, I pay USD 100 for CLF-C02. Passing it gives me a voucher, so SAA-C03 costs USD 75 instead of USD 150. Passing SAA-C03 gives another voucher, so SAP-C02 costs USD 150 instead of USD 300. That is USD 325 instead of USD 550, before local taxes. The voucher saves the most on expensive exams. Some people therefore save one voucher for a Professional exam. I would check the voucher's expiry date and terms in the Benefits section. The voucher comes only from a pass, so it does not help with a retake after a failure.
keyPoints: Each pass earns a 50% voucher in the Benefits section
Example costs: 100 + 75 + 150 = USD 325 instead of 550
Use it on higher-priced exams for the biggest saving
Check the voucher terms and expiry; it is not earned from a fail

subjective.question: List your exam-day checklist for an online proctored AWS exam.
subjective.answer: The day before, I run the Pearson VUE system test on the same laptop and network I will use. I close VPNs and background apps, and I keep the laptop plugged in. I prepare a private, quiet room with a clear desk: no notes, phones within reach, or second monitors. I keep my government ID ready and confirm that the name exactly matches my AWS Certification Account. On the day, I start check-in early. Check-in needs photos of my face, my ID and my workspace. I tell family not to enter the room. During the exam I stay in camera view, do not read questions aloud, and keep my hands away from my face. I plan as though there are no breaks, so I eat and use the washroom before I start.
keyPoints: Run the system test on the exact machine and network
Private, clear room with no extra devices or people
ID name exactly matches the account name
Check in early and follow the proctor rules throughout

subjective.question: You failed an AWS Associate exam. Describe your recovery plan.
subjective.answer: First I read the score report in my AWS Certification Account. It shows my scaled score and which domains need improvement. Because scoring is compensatory, I focus on the weakest domains, which will lift my overall score fastest. I must wait 14 days before retaking, and I pay the full fee again because vouchers come only from passing. So I treat the retake as a fresh investment. I plan two to four weeks of targeted revision. That includes hands-on labs for weak services, rereading the exam guide and doing timed practice sets to fix pacing. I review why each wrong practice answer was wrong, not just what the right answer was. I book the retake only when my practice scores are steady, and I recheck ESL and ID details before booking.
keyPoints: Use the score report to find weak domains
Wait 14 days and pay the full fee for the retake
Do targeted hands-on revision and timed practice
Book only when practice results are stable

subjective.question: Why does the name on your ID matter so much, and how do you prevent problems?
subjective.answer: At check-in, the proctor or test centre staff compare my government ID with the name in my AWS Certification Account. They must match exactly. If they do not, I can be turned away, and I lose the exam fee. In India this often happens with initials, surnames written in different orders, or missing middle names. For example, the passport says 'S. Lakshmi Narayanan' but the account says 'Lakshmi Narayanan'. To prevent it, I choose the ID I will carry, usually a passport for consistency. I set my account name to match it exactly, letter for letter. I do this well before exam day, not the night before. I also check that the ID is valid and not expired, and that the photo is clear.
keyPoints: The ID name must exactly match the account name
A mismatch can mean being turned away and losing the fee
Watch for initials, name order and middle names
Fix it well before exam day using the ID you will carry

subjective.question: Explain the reschedule and cancellation rules and how they affect your booking strategy.
subjective.answer: I can reschedule or cancel without losing the fee only if I do it more than 24 hours before the appointment. If I miss that window or do not turn up, the fee is lost. That can be USD 150 for an Associate exam or USD 300 for a Professional exam. So I set a calendar reminder about two days before the exam. At that point I make a go or no-go decision based on my latest timed practice scores. I avoid booking during busy work weeks, festivals or travel. For online exams, I also rerun the system test before the 24-hour cutoff. That way, if my setup fails, I can still move to another slot or a test centre without losing the fee.
keyPoints: Change the booking more than 24 hours before to keep the fee
A no-show or late change loses the fee
Make a go or no-go check before the cutoff
Test the online setup early enough to switch if needed

subjective.question: How do you claim and use your Credly badge professionally?
subjective.answer: After my result is released in my AWS Certification Account, usually within 5 business days, I get an email from Credly to claim my badge. I accept it using the email linked to my certification. The badge shows the certification name, the issue date and the expiry date. Anyone can verify it through its public link. I add it to LinkedIn under Licenses & certifications and share the verification link. On my résumé, I list the full official name, for example 'AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03)', with the date and the Credly link. Recruiters prefer a verifiable link to a screenshot. When I recertify, the badge updates, so the public record stays current.
keyPoints: The Credly email follows the result release
The badge is publicly verifiable and shows the issue and expiry dates
Add it to LinkedIn and the résumé with the official name and link
It updates after recertification

subjective.question: How would you manage time on SAA-C03, with and without ESL?
subjective.answer: SAA-C03 has 65 questions in 130 minutes, which is 2 minutes per question. With ESL it is 160 minutes, close to 2.5 minutes per question. I aim to finish a first pass with around 20 minutes left. I answer quickly when I am confident. For long scenarios, I read the last line first to see what is being asked, such as the most cost-effective or the least operational overhead option. Then I remove the clearly wrong options. If I am stuck, I pick my best guess, flag the question and move on, because there is no negative marking. In the review pass, I revisit only the flagged questions. I do not change answers without a clear reason. Practising timed sets beforehand makes this pacing feel natural.
keyPoints: 130 min = about 2 min per question; 160 min with ESL
Read the requirement first and remove wrong options
Guess, flag and move on; no negative marking
Leave time for a review of flagged questions

subjective.question: Interview question: How do you keep your AWS skills current between recertifications?
subjective.answer: The certificate lasts 3 years, but AWS changes every month, so I don't wait for the recertification deadline. I follow AWS What's New and the release announcements for the services I use. I read the Well-Architected Framework updates, because exam scenarios and design reviews are based on them. I do small hands-on labs in a sandbox account with budget alerts set, so I can try new features safely. At work, I apply new features when they cut cost or effort, for example moving workloads to newer instance families or managed services. When an exam version changes, I compare the old and new exam guides to find the gaps. This way recertification is a quick check, not a fresh start, and my day-to-day work improves too.
keyPoints: Follow AWS announcements and Well-Architected updates
Use a sandbox account with budget alerts for hands-on practice
Apply new features at work where they add value
Compare exam guide versions before recertifying

subjective.question: Describe your plan for the final exam week before an AWS certification exam.
subjective.answer: Early in the week I confirm the logistics. My ESL approval, if it applies, is done before booking. The booking is confirmed. My ID name matches my account. For online delivery, the system test has passed. I then do one full-length timed practice exam: 90, 130 or 180 minutes depending on the level, plus 30 minutes if I have ESL. I spend the next days reviewing the wrong answers and my weak domains from the exam guide, not learning new topics from scratch. Two days out, before the 24-hour reschedule cutoff, I decide whether to go ahead. The day before, I only revise lightly, prepare my room or travel plan, and sleep well. On exam day I check in early and stay calm.
keyPoints: Confirm ESL, booking, ID match and system test early
One full timed mock using the correct duration
Review weak domains; avoid new topics
Go or no-go decision before the 24-hour cutoff

subjective.question: A manager asks you to plan certification for a 10-person team over a year. What policies and risks would you explain?
subjective.answer: I would explain the rules that affect cost and schedule. Each person needs an AWS Certification Account with a name that exactly matches their ID, or they risk losing the fee at check-in. Non-native English speakers should request ESL before booking, because it applies only to exams scheduled after approval. Each pass gives a 50% voucher, so a path like Cloud Practitioner, then an Associate, then a Professional gets cheaper at each step. Failures cost the full fee again, with a 14-day wait, so I would budget for some retakes. Bookings must change more than 24 hours ahead, or the fee is lost. Certifications are valid for 3 years, so I would track expiry dates for each person and plan recertification on the current exam version well before they expire.
keyPoints: ID name match and ESL before booking for each person
Use 50% vouchers along the path
Budget for retakes at full fee and the 14-day wait
Track 3-year expiry dates and plan recertification

subjective.question: Written question: Explain the full lifecycle of an AWS certification, from account creation to recertification.
subjective.answer: I create an AWS Certification Account and make sure my name exactly matches my government ID. If English is not my first language, I request the ESL accommodation and wait for approval. Then I book through Pearson VUE, choosing online proctoring (OnVUE) or a test centre. I can reschedule or cancel more than 24 hours before without losing the fee. I sit the exam: 90 minutes for Foundational, 130 for Associate and 180 for Professional, plus 30 with ESL. Scoring is scaled from 100 to 1000, with pass marks of 700, 720 or 750. Results usually appear within 5 business days. After a pass, I claim my Credly badge and find a 50% voucher in Benefits. After a fail, I wait 14 days and pay again. The certification lasts 3 years, and I recertify by passing the current version before it expires.
keyPoints: Account set-up with an exact ID name match, and ESL before booking
Pearson VUE delivery choice and the 24-hour change rule
Exam lengths, scaled scoring and pass marks by level
Results, Credly badge, 50% voucher, 14-day retake and 3-year validity

subjective.question: Your OnVUE system test fails on exam morning. The exam starts in 90 minutes. Walk through how you would troubleshoot and what your fallback is.
subjective.answer: First, I check the most common causes. I turn off any VPN or proxy and close every other application, including messaging and screen-sharing tools, plus background sync apps. I also make sure only one monitor is connected. If I am on a corporate laptop, I switch to a personal machine, because endpoint security policies often block the secure browser. Next, I check the network. I move closer to the router or use a mobile hotspot, and I re-run the bandwidth part of the test. I also check that the webcam and microphone are not being used by another app and that browser permissions are granted. If it still fails, I contact Pearson VUE support straight away. I do not wait until the check-in window opens. If the exam is still more than 24 hours away, which is not the case here, rescheduling is the safe choice. Inside 24 hours, I document everything and raise a case with Pearson VUE and AWS Training and Certification support. The real lesson: run the system test days earlier, on the same device and network.
keyPoints: Disable VPN/proxy and close background apps; use a single monitor
Prefer a personal machine over a locked-down corporate laptop
Check bandwidth, webcam and microphone permissions
Contact Pearson VUE support early and document the issue
Prevention: run the system test days earlier on the same setup

subjective.question: A colleague scored 690 on SAA-C03. The report shows 'Needs improvement' in Design Resilient Architectures and Design High-Performing Architectures. How would you interpret this and plan the retake?

code.code:
Scaled score: 690 (pass mark 720)
Design Secure Architectures ............ Meets competencies
Design Resilient Architectures ......... Needs improvement
Design High-Performing Architectures ... Needs improvement
Design Cost-Optimized Architectures .... Meets competencies

subjective.answer: 690 is close to the 720 pass mark on a 100–1000 scale, so the gap is narrow and focused. Scoring is compensatory, so he does not need to perfect every domain. But two weak domains pulled the total down. Resilient design covers Multi-AZ, Auto Scaling, decoupling with SQS and SNS, backups and disaster recovery strategies. High-performing design covers caching, storage and database selection, and network performance. These two domains carry a large share of the exam weighting, so improving them gives the biggest gain. My plan: he waits the mandatory 14 days before retaking. He spends two to three weeks on targeted hands-on labs in those areas. He takes timed practice sets and reviews why each wrong option is wrong. He books the retake only when he scores well above the pass mark on practice tests.
