He pays the full fee again, so the retake should be a planned decision, not a reaction.
keyPoints: 690 vs 720 pass mark: a narrow gap
Compensatory scoring: improve the weak, high-weight domains
Map weak sections to concrete topics and hands-on labs
14-day wait before retake; the full fee applies
Book the retake when practice scores are comfortably above passing

subjective.question: Your company is an AWS Partner and needs a minimum number of active certified staff. Your Developer – Associate certification expired last week. What do you tell your manager, and what do you do?
subjective.answer: I tell my manager plainly: the certification has expired, my Credly badge now shows as expired, and it no longer counts as active for our partner requirements. AWS has no paid renewal and no grace period for the credential itself. The only fix is to pass the current version of DVA-C02, or whichever version is live, again. I check the current exam guide for changes since I last passed, because services and domains get updated. Then I give a firm date: about two to three weeks of focused revision, followed by the booking. If I hold a 50% voucher from a recent pass, I use it to cut the cost. To stop this happening again, I suggest a shared tracker of every team member's expiry dates, with reminders about six months ahead. People then recertify early instead of letting certifications lapse.
keyPoints: Expired means not counted; the badge shows as expired
No paid renewal or grace period; pass the current version
Review the current exam guide for changes
Give a concrete recertification date and use the voucher if available
Prevent repeats with an expiry tracker and early reminders

subjective.question: AWS announces a new version of the exam you are studying for. The current version retires in a few months. How do you decide whether to book the current version or wait?
subjective.answer: First, I read both exam guides side by side and compare the domains, the weightings and the in-scope services. If I am already near exam-ready on the current version, I book it before it retires. My material matches it, and the certification I earn is the same credential, valid for 3 years either way. If I am still early in my study, I check whether the new version changes a lot of content. If it does, I switch my study plan to the new guide so I am not learning retiring topics. I also keep in mind that early study resources for a new version are usually limited. Third-party mock exams may lag behind. I avoid booking close to the retirement date, because I would lose the option to retake on the same version. Whichever version I choose, I book through the AWS Certification Account, and I confirm my ESL accommodation is in place first.
keyPoints: Compare the old and new exam guides: domains, weightings, services
If near-ready, book the current version before retirement
If early in study, align with the new version
Avoid booking right before retirement, so there is time to retake
Book through the AWS Certification Account with accommodations in place

subjective.question: Halfway through an OnVUE exam, your internet drops and the exam window freezes. What should you do, and what should you avoid?
subjective.answer: I stay at my desk and stay in camera view. I do not use my phone to browse or open any other application, because that can look like misconduct. I try to restore the connection, for example by restarting the router or switching to a mobile hotspot. Then I relaunch the OnVUE application if prompted, because the proctor may be able to reconnect me and resume the exam. If the session cannot be resumed, I contact Pearson VUE support as soon as possible. I note the time, what happened and any error messages. Then I open a case with AWS Training and Certification support and include the Pearson VUE case number, so they can review options such as a reschedule. What I avoid: leaving the room, talking to people, or trying to take notes about exam questions. Exam content is covered by the candidate agreement and must never be shared or recorded.
keyPoints: Stay in view; do not use other devices or apps
Restore the connection and relaunch OnVUE; the proctor may resume the exam
Contact Pearson VUE support and record times and errors
Open an AWS Training and Certification case with reference numbers
Never record or share exam content

subjective.question: A friend offers you a PDF of 'real AWS exam questions' a week before your SAA-C03 exam. How do you respond, and why?
subjective.answer: I decline. Before every AWS exam, candidates accept the AWS Certification Program Agreement, which includes a non-disclosure agreement covering exam content. Using or sharing leaked questions breaks that agreement. AWS can revoke certifications, ban candidates from future exams and invalidate results. Beyond the rules, dumps are often wrong or out of date. Questions are drawn from a large pool, and unscored items keep changing, so memorising answers is a poor bet. More importantly, the certification has value only if I can do the work. Interviews will test scenario reasoning, not recall. I would rather use legitimate resources: the official exam guide and sample questions, AWS Skill Builder practice material, hands-on labs, and good third-party mock tests that teach the reasoning behind each answer.
keyPoints: The candidate agreement/NDA forbids using or sharing exam content
Consequences: revocation, bans, invalidated results
Dumps are often inaccurate; question pools change
Real value comes from skills tested in interviews
Use the official exam guide, sample questions, Skill Builder and labs

subjective.question: How should you approach the multiple-response, ordering and matching questions that appear on newer AWS exams such as AIF-C01 and MLA-C01?
subjective.answer: All of these question types are all-or-nothing. A multiple-response question earns credit only if I select every correct option, and the question states how many to choose. Ordering and matching questions need the full sequence or every pairing to be correct. So I slow down on them. For multiple-response, I evaluate each option on its own as true or false against the scenario, instead of looking for 'the best two'. For ordering, I first identify the step that must come first and the step that must come last, then fill the middle using dependencies. For example, data must be prepared before training, and training must happen before deployment. For matching, I start with the pairs I am sure of, then use elimination for the rest. I still never leave anything blank, because there is no penalty for guessing. If a question takes too long, I flag it and return to it later.
keyPoints: All-or-nothing credit; no partial marks
Judge each multiple-response option independently
Ordering: anchor the first and last steps, then use dependencies
Matching: fix the certain pairs first, then eliminate
Never leave blanks; flag and return when slow

subjective.question: You plan to take an OnVUE exam from an office meeting room on a Sunday evening, because your home is noisy. What risks do you check before booking?
subjective.answer: OnVUE needs a private, quiet room where nobody enters during the exam. On a Sunday, I need to confirm that cleaners, security staff or colleagues will not walk in. A person entering the room can end the exam. Glass walls and whiteboards are a problem. Whiteboards must be wiped clean or covered, and people passing by in view may be flagged. The desk must be clear, and I can have no second monitor, notes or phone within reach. The office network is my biggest worry, because corporate firewalls and proxies often block OnVUE. So I run the system test in that exact room, on that network and on the device I will use, ideally a personal laptop. I also check the building's power backup and access hours, so I am not locked out mid-exam. If I cannot meet these conditions, a Pearson VUE test centre is the safer choice.
keyPoints: The room must be private, with no interruptions
Clear the desk and whiteboards; watch glass walls
Corporate network and device restrictions can block OnVUE
Run the system test in the exact room, on the same network and device
Fall back to a test centre if conditions are uncertain

subjective.question: A hiring manager asks how they can trust that an 'AWS Certified' line on a résumé is real and current. Explain the verification options and what to look for.
subjective.answer: AWS issues digital badges through Credly. A genuine badge has a public URL on Credly that shows the holder's name, the exact certification, the issue date and the expiry date. It also shows whether the badge is active or expired. I would ask the candidate for their Credly link rather than a PDF or screenshot, since images can be edited. AWS also offers certification validation: the candidate can share their validation number, which confirms the credential with AWS directly. Things to check: the name matches the candidate's ID, and the certification is the current one the role needs. A Cloud Practitioner badge is not the same as Solutions Architect – Professional. Also check that the expiry date has not passed, because AWS certifications are valid for 3 years. Finally, I would back the badge with scenario interview questions. The certification proves exam knowledge, and the interview proves the person can apply it.
keyPoints: Ask for the Credly badge URL, not screenshots
AWS validation number for direct confirmation
Check the name, the exact certification and active/expiry status
Certifications are valid for 3 years
Confirm practical skill with scenario interviews

subjective.question: Case study: Aditya works in Pune. He is a non-native English speaker. His home is noisy, and his office laptop is locked down with a VPN. His 50% voucher expires in six weeks, and his SAA-C03 certification expires in three months. He wants to pass SAP-C02. Build his plan.
subjective.answer: I would first log in to the AWS Certification Account and confirm the profile name matches his ID exactly. Then I would request the ESL accommodation and wait for approval before booking anything. With ESL, SAP-C02 becomes 210 minutes. His home is noisy and the office laptop is risky, so I would book a Pearson VUE test centre in Pune. He should apply the voucher at payment, well before its expiry date. Passing SAP-C02 recertifies SAA-C03, so he should aim for an exam date at least a few weeks before the SAA expiry. That leaves room to retake after the 14-day wait if needed. As a fallback, if he fails twice, he books the current SAA-C03 before expiry so the Associate does not lapse. After passing, he claims the Credly badge and updates his résumé.
keyPoints: ESL approved before booking, giving 210 minutes on SAP-C02
Test centre removes the noise, VPN and laptop risk
Voucher applied at booking, before it expires
SAP-C02 recertifies SAA-C03 only if passed before expiry, with a retake buffer

subjective.question: Troubleshooting: A candidate says, 'My ESL was approved months ago, my last exam history is missing, and my voucher is not showing.' What is the likely cause, and how do you fix it?
subjective.answer: The likely cause is a duplicate AWS Certification Account. People often create a second account after losing access to the first, or by signing in with a different email, such as a personal one instead of a work one. ESL approval, exam history, vouchers and badges all belong to one account. The new account sees none of them. To confirm this, I would sign in with each email the candidate has used and compare the exam history. The fix is to contact AWS Training and Certification support and ask them to merge the accounts, before booking anything new. If the exam is booked on the wrong account, it may run without ESL and without the voucher. After the merge, I would check that the profile name matches the ID, that ESL shows as approved and that the voucher appears under Benefits.
keyPoints: Duplicate accounts split history, ESL, vouchers and badges
Confirm by signing in with each email used
Ask AWS Training and Certification support to merge the accounts
Do not book until the merged account shows ESL and the voucher

subjective.question: Comparison: To keep your Solutions Architect – Associate active, is it better to retake the current SAA-C03 or pass SAP-C02? Explain when each one wins.
subjective.answer: Both keep the Associate active. Passing the current SAA-C03 renews it. Passing SAP-C02 earns the Professional certification and also recertifies the Associate. SAP-C02 is better value if you are already working at that level. You get two active certifications from one exam, and the Professional carries more weight in interviews. It is harder, though. It has 75 questions in 180 minutes, costs USD 300 and needs a pass mark of 750. Retaking SAA-C03 is better when time is short or your recent work has not reached Professional depth. It is cheaper and more predictable. My rule is this: if expiry is more than four months away and I am ready, I attempt SAP-C02. If expiry is close, I take SAA-C03 first so nothing lapses, then do SAP-C02 later. Either way, I use my 50% voucher.
keyPoints: Both options recertify the Associate
SAP-C02 earns a second certification but is harder and costs more
SAA-C03 is the safer choice when expiry is close
Choose based on time to expiry and how ready you are

subjective.question: Put these post-exam steps in the right order and explain why: add the badge to LinkedIn and your résumé, accept the Credly invitation, note the voucher expiry, receive the result email, and set a recertification reminder.
subjective.answer: The order is: receive the result email, accept the Credly invitation, add the badge to LinkedIn and your résumé, note the voucher expiry, and set a recertification reminder. Results usually arrive within five business days, and the Credly invitation follows. You accept it with the email linked to your Certification Account. Only after accepting do you have a public, verifiable badge URL. That URL is what you add to LinkedIn and your résumé, because recruiters prefer a link they can check. Next, open Benefits and note when the 50% voucher expires, so you can schedule your next exam in time. Finally, add a calendar reminder about six months before the three-year expiry. That gives room to prepare, pass and retake if needed.
keyPoints: The result comes first, then the Credly invitation
Share the badge only after accepting it, so the link is verifiable
Check the voucher expiry in Benefits
Set the recertification reminder months ahead

subjective.question: Spot every mistake in this account and booking plan, and correct each one.

code.code:
Week -4: Lost old login, so create a new Certification Account with work email
Week -4: Book SAA-C03 on OnVUE for a Saturday
Week -3: Request ESL accommodation
Week -2: Set profile name to 'Sunny Sharma' (passport: Sunil Kumar Sharma)
Week -1: Plan to apply the 50% voucher at check-in on exam day

subjective.answer: There are four mistakes. First, creating a new account instead of recovering the old one splits his history and his voucher. He should recover the old account or ask support to merge the two. Second, booking in week -4 and requesting ESL in week -3 is the wrong order. The booking keeps the standard 130 minutes, so he would have to reschedule after approval. He should request ESL first, then book. Third, 'Sunny Sharma' does not match the passport. The profile must read 'Sunil Kumar Sharma', or he may be refused admission. He should fix this well before exam day. Fourth, the voucher is applied during payment when you book, not at check-in. If he waits until exam day, he either pays full price or the voucher expires. The corrected order is: recover the account, fix the name, get ESL approved, then book with the voucher.
keyPoints: A duplicate account splits history and vouchers
Request ESL before booking
The profile name must match the ID exactly
The voucher is applied at booking and payment

subjective.question: Troubleshooting: The OnVUE system test passed on Thursday, but on Saturday morning the exam will not launch. What are the likely causes, and how do you investigate?
subjective.answer:
Something changed between Thursday and Saturday, so I look for the difference. The most common causes are these:
- A different network, such as a hotspot or another room's Wi-Fi
- A VPN or security agent that reconnected automatically
- An operating system or antivirus update that installed overnight
- Background apps like Teams, OneDrive or screen recorders that the OnVUE app flags
- Low bandwidth because others at home are streaming
- Camera or microphone permissions reset by an update

I would restart the machine, disconnect any VPN, close every background app, and switch to the same network I tested on, wired if possible. Then I rerun the system test, not just the launch. Prevention matters more. Run the test again on exam morning, pause updates and ask others to stay off the network. If it still fails, contact Pearson VUE support before the start time.
keyPoints: Find what changed: network, VPN, updates or apps
Rerun the full system test after each fix
Use the exact tested setup, and pause updates beforehand
Contact Pearson VUE support early if it still fails

subjective.question: Comparison: Is it better to book your exam for a fixed date four weeks away now, or to study until you feel ready and then book? Justify your choice.
subjective.answer: I prefer booking a fixed date, with conditions. A booked date creates a real deadline. It also secures a convenient slot, because test centre slots in Indian cities can fill up, especially at weekends. It also makes you plan backwards: request ESL first, use the voucher before it expires, and finish full practice tests by the second-last week. The risk is booking too early. Rescheduling is free only if you do it more than 24 hours before the appointment, so I would set a checkpoint one week before the exam. If my practice scores are not clearly above the pass level, I reschedule then, not on the last day. 'Study until ready' suits people with very unpredictable workloads, but it often leads to delay and expired vouchers. A fixed date with a review checkpoint gives you discipline and keeps your options open.
keyPoints: A fixed date creates a deadline and secures a slot
Request ESL before booking
Reschedule more than 24 hours ahead to avoid losing the fee
A one-week checkpoint using practice test scores

subjective.question: Case study: You will sit DOP-C02 with ESL, which makes it 210 minutes. Which delivery method do you choose for such a long exam, and how do you prepare physically and logistically?
subjective.answer: For a 210-minute exam, I lean towards a test centre. Online proctored AWS exams do not allow breaks. Over three and a half hours, the risk of noise, power cuts, Wi-Fi drops or someone entering the room grows. A test centre controls all of that. If I must use OnVUE, I need a reliable room, a UPS for power cuts, a wired connection and family support for the whole period. Either way, I eat a light meal, drink water at a sensible time and use the washroom just before check-in. I practise full-length 75-question mock exams under timed conditions to build stamina. My pacing is roughly 2.8 minutes per question, with checkpoints such as question 25 by about 70 minutes. I keep 20 to 25 minutes for flagged questions. I answer every question, since there is no penalty for guessing.
keyPoints: Long exams increase the risks of OnVUE, so prefer a test centre
No breaks online, so prepare physically
Full-length timed mock exams for stamina
Pacing checkpoints, and answer every question

subjective.question: Spot the mistakes in this team certification tracker. It is March 2026.

code.code:
Name    | Cert      | Passed     | Expiry     | Note
Asha    | SAA-C03   | 2024-05-10 | 2026-05-10 | Book retake urgently
Rohit   | CLF-C02   | 2023-02-01 | 2026-02-01 | EXPIRED (also passed DVA-C02 on 2025-01-15)
Imran   | Voucher   | 2026-01-20 | check      | Use for Azure AZ-104
Lakshmi | DVA-C02   | 2023-09-01 | 2026-09-01 | Will recertify by passing DEA-C01

subjective.answer: Asha's expiry is wrong. Certifications last three years, so a May 2024 pass expires in May 2027, and there is no urgency. Rohit's CLF is not expired. Passing DVA-C02 in January 2025 recertified his Cloud Practitioner, so it now runs to around January 2028. Imran's note is wrong because the 50% voucher applies only to AWS exams, not to Azure or any other vendor. Also, 'check' is not an expiry date. The team should record the real expiry from the Benefits section. Lakshmi's plan fails. DEA-C01 is a different Associate and does not recertify Developer – Associate. She must pass the current DVA-C02 or DOP-C02 before September 2026. My fix is to pull the dates from each person's Certification Account or Credly profile instead of working them out by hand.
keyPoints: Validity is three years from the pass date
A higher-level pass recertifies Cloud Practitioner
Vouchers are AWS-only and have real expiry dates
DEA-C01 does not recertify DVA; use DVA-C02 or DOP-C02

subjective.question: Troubleshooting: A candidate's OnVUE exam was ended by the proctor. The candidate says, 'I did nothing wrong.' How would you work out what happened, and what are the next steps?
subjective.answer:
I would replay the session from the candidate's side, because proctors act on what the camera and microphone pick up. Common triggers are:
- Reading questions aloud or muttering
- Looking away from the screen often, for example at a second screen or notes
- Someone entering the room or speaking nearby
- Leaving the camera view or covering the face
- A phone ringing within reach
- Banned items on the desk
- Running unapproved software

Often the candidate did these things without meaning to, such as thinking aloud. Next, they should read the email from Pearson VUE and AWS, which usually states the reason. They should then raise a case with AWS Training and Certification support through the Certification Account, giving the appointment details and any facts, such as a household interruption. A refund or free retake is not guaranteed. For the next attempt, I would recommend a test centre or a stricter room routine and silent reading practice.
keyPoints: Proctors act on what the camera and microphone record
Common causes: reading aloud, looking away, interruptions
Raise a case with AWS Training and Certification support
A refund is not guaranteed; fix the setup next time

subjective.question: Interview question: You hold SAA-C03 (expires Oct 2027), DVA-C02 (expires Mar 2027) and DEA-C01 (expires Jan 2028). How do you keep all three active with the fewest exams and still grow?
subjective.answer: I map which exams recertify which certifications. DOP-C02 recertifies Developer – Associate, so I would target it before March 2027, ideally by late 2026 to leave time for a retake. That one exam renews DVA and adds a Professional. Next is SAA, which expires in October 2027. SAP-C02 recertifies it and adds a second Professional, so I would aim for mid-2027, using the voucher from my DOP pass. DEA-C01 has no Professional above it in this path, so I would pass the current DEA version during 2027. I would also check for exam version changes first. So the total is three exams, which give two new Professionals and three renewed certifications. Each pass gives a 50% voucher for the next exam. I keep the expiry dates in a calendar with six-month reminders, and I check the current exam guides because versions change.
keyPoints: DOP-C02 recertifies DVA; SAP-C02 recertifies SAA
Sequence the exams by expiry date, leaving retake buffers
Chain the 50% vouchers between exams
Check the current exam versions before booking

subjective.question: Spot the mistakes in this exam-day timeline for a 10:00 OnVUE exam.

code.code:
08:30  Laptop shows 'Updates pending', choose 'Restart later'
09:50  Open OnVUE app and begin check-in
09:52  Connect earbuds to listen to calm music during check-in
09:55  Phone kept face down on desk for emergencies
10:00  Exam starts
11:00  Step out to refill water bottle, back in 1 minute

subjective.answer: There are five problems. First, pending updates are a risk. They can force a restart in the middle of the exam. He should install them the day before and rerun the system test. Second, starting check-in at 09:50 is late. Check-in opens at 09:30 and includes ID and room photos, so he should start then. Third, earbuds are not allowed at any point during an online proctored exam. Fourth, the phone must not be on the desk. It should be out of arm's reach, silent and only used if the proctor needs to contact him. Fifth, stepping out at 11:00 breaks the rules. Online AWS exams allow no breaks, and leaving the camera view can end the exam with no refund. He should keep water off the desk unless the rules allow it, and use the washroom before check-in.
keyPoints: Install updates the day before and retest
Start check-in 30 minutes early
No earbuds, and the phone out of reach
No breaks during online AWS exams

subjective.question: Troubleshooting: A learner says, 'I passed DEA-C01 last year, so my SAA-C03 should be renewed, but Credly shows SAA as expired.' What went wrong, and what now?
subjective.answer: The assumption was wrong. Passing an exam renews only that certification and any certification below it in the same path. DEA-C01 is a separate Associate, and it does not recertify Solutions Architect – Associate. Only passing the current SAA-C03, or SAP-C02 while SAA is still active, would have renewed it. Now that SAA has expired, it cannot be revived. The learner must pass the current SAA exam as a new candidate. Their DEA-C01 stays valid. I would also check two other causes. One is a duplicate Certification Account, where a recertification sits on a different account. The other is a Credly email mismatch, where the new badge went to another inbox. For the future, I would build a simple map showing which exam renews which certification, and set reminders months before each expiry.
keyPoints: An exam renews only its own certification and the ones below it
DEA-C01 does not recertify SAA
An expired certification means passing the exam again as a new candidate
Rule out duplicate accounts and Credly email problems

subjective.question: Comparison: Your English is good, but it is not your first language. Is it better to request ESL or skip it? Discuss the trade-offs.
subjective.answer: If you are eligible because English is not your primary language, I would request it. Many Indian learners qualify. The extra 30 minutes costs nothing, and it does not change your score or appear on your certificate. AWS questions are long scenarios with similar-looking options. Extra time helps you read carefully and review flagged questions. That matters most on Professional exams, which have 75 questions. There are only small downsides. First, you must request ESL before booking, so it adds a step to planning. Second, the longer session means more stamina is needed, and online exams allow no breaks, so plan for that. You do not have to use all the time either. You can submit early. Skipping ESL only makes sense if you are not eligible. Then you should rely on timed practice. Never request ESL after booking, or you will have to reschedule.
keyPoints: Free extra time with no effect on the score
Request it once, before booking
A longer session needs stamina with no breaks online
Submitting early is allowed

subjective.question: Case study: Divya passed AIF-C01. Her 50% voucher expires in five weeks, but she will not be ready for SAA-C03 for about three months. What are her options, and which do you recommend?
subjective.answer: Option one: let the voucher expire and pay full price later. This is simple but wastes about USD 75. Option two: use it now on an exam she can realistically pass soon. This only makes sense if she already has strong skills for another Associate, such as DEA-C01 or MLA-C01. Option three: apply the voucher at booking and pick a later SAA-C03 date. This only works if the voucher terms allow the exam to fall after the expiry date. Whether expiry is tied to the booking date or the exam date depends on the terms, so she must read them in the Benefits section first. I would recommend option three if the terms allow it, choosing a date about three months out with rescheduling more than 24 hours ahead. If they do not, she should not rush SAA-C03 just to save USD 75, because a fail costs more. Next time, she should plan the next exam before her current pass.
keyPoints: The voucher has a fixed expiry date
Check whether expiry applies to the booking or the exam date
Do not rush an exam just to save on a voucher
Plan the next exam before the current one

subjective.question: Interview question: You passed SAA-C03 with 735, and the domain breakdown shows 'Needs improvement' in Design Cost-Optimized Architectures. The interviewer asks if that worries you. How do you answer?
subjective.answer: I would be honest. AWS uses a compensatory scoring model. The pass is based on the overall scaled score of 720 or above, not on each domain. So I passed fairly, but the report showed cost optimisation as my weaker area. I took that as a learning signal, not a weakness to hide. Since the exam, I have worked on it in practice. I used Cost Explorer and AWS Budgets in my sandbox account. I compared Savings Plans with Reserved Instances, chose S3 storage classes and lifecycle rules, and right-sized instances using Compute Optimizer. I can walk them through a recent example where I cut costs. I would also mention that domain feedback is broad, so I treat it as a direction rather than a precise measure. This shows I understand the scoring model and act on the feedback.
keyPoints: Compensatory model: the overall scaled score decides the pass
Domain feedback is a broad direction, not a precise score
Show the concrete hands-on work done since the exam
Name specific cost tools and decisions
